title: Tobacco Taxes Prove Something About Marijuana Prohibition That Politicians Need to Learn

content_html_sanitized:
Reason, the great libertarian publication, recently reported “With Cigarette Taxes Sky High, More New Yorkers Than Ever Turn to the Black Market. In New York City, just one in six cigarette packs collected by researchers came through legal channels.”

(In the United States, cigarettes are taxed federally at rate of $1.01 per pack, but each state sets its own rate.)

 

In New York City the combined Federal, state and various local taxes have risen to a combined $12.00 per pack, with the result that almost 85% are “bootleg”, to borrow a term from another economic fiasco.

 

In fact, New York City, with its large Irish, Italian, and Jewish population, largely ignored alcohol prohibition, which was imposed by the Protestant “heartland”.

 

It also largely ignored marijuana Prohibition until Giuliani.

See Implosion of Giuliani Fraud Would Not Be Ordinarily On Topic for MarijuanaNews, but…

 

The result has not only been a loss of revenue, it has also created a huge black market and a contraband culture around the sale of single cigarettes called Loosies.

 

So, surprise, surprise, when there was a delay in authorizing the new legal marijuana stores, the number of illegal stores exploded. Now the licensing process is catching up, the City is forcing the closure of the unlicensed stores.

See Growing like a weed: Legal cannabis shops in NY will soar to sky-high 625 in 2025, regulators say

 

The obvious question remains. Will the City overtax cannabis the way it has tobacco? The black market is already there.

 

Meanwhile, with a touch of irony, this story from The Netherlands, also hit this week.

Dutch Finance Ministry: higher tobacco taxes yield no extra revenue: “The Dutch government’s tobacco tax hikes no longer increase state revenue, largely due to cross-border cigarette purchases, according to a Ministry of Finance report published on Prinsjesdag. Previously, the ministry expected that a 5-cent tax increase per pack would add 7 million euros to the treasury. That amount is now projected at zero.”

 

“The art of taxation is the art of plucking the goose so as to get the most feathers with the least hissing.” Jean-Baptiste Colbert.
